per_article_summaries: Kimi Antonelli became the second-youngest driver to win an F1 race at the Chinese Grand Prix. Alex Brundle has identified a weakness for the 19-year-old. Brundle believes Antonelli has the pace to challenge George Russell for the championship.

Mercedes leads the constructors' standings with 98 points, 31 points more than Ferrari in second. Former Haas F1 team principal Guenther Steiner believes Mercedes will face threats from other teams this year. The next round of the F1 season will take place at the Suzuka Circuit for the Japanese Grand Prix.

Ollie Bearman watched his former Formula 2 team-mate clinch his first grand prix victory at the Chinese Grand Prix at the Shanghai International Circuit. The Briton said it gave him confidence that he would be able to reach the same milestone one day. Bearman currently sits fifth in the drivers' standings with 17 points.

Lewis Hamilton has returned to form after a difficult few years. The seven-time champion struggled to adapt to the ground effect cars. He has also been tasked with adjusting to his new surroundings at Ferrari. The Briton currently sits fourth in the drivers' standings.
Oscar Piastri has yet to start a grand prix for McLaren in 2026. Lando Norris didn't even get as far as the grid in China. It was the first time neither McLaren has started a grand prix since 2005.

Oscar Piastri set the pace with a 1m30.133s, finishing around a tenth clear of the two Mercedes drivers, Kimi Antonelli and George Russell. Mercedes once again proved to be the dominant force, and by a clear margin. The key difference lies on the long straights in sectors one and three.

Ferrari lost close to four tenths on Suzuka's home straight and into Turn 1. Hamilton and Leclerc were also struggling with the SF-26's tricky balance. Ferrari's sporting director Diego Ioverno felt the deficit was largely as expected.

Mercedes F1 driver Kimi Antonelli has headed team-mate George Russell in final practice at the Japanese Grand Prix. Russell was unable to top Antonelli's final quarter lap in the W17 as Mercedes heads to qualifying as the clear favourites. Oscar Piastri was fourth, one second in arrears, narrowly ahead of the second Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton.

Ferrari's SF-26 has a slightly different performance envelope to the Mercedes W17. It seems to have a slightly better mechanical balance and more downforce. This, along with a highly effective straightline mode, enables the drivers to super clip earlier on long straights.

Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Alex Albon, Sergio Perez, Liam Lawson and Carlos Sainz were under the spotlight. All incidents resulted in no further action at Suzuka. Hamilton was under investigation for Article B1.8.5 of the sporting regulations. Verstappen also told stewards that he didn't consider it a dangerous situation.

Championship leader George Russell has topped Formula 1's first free practice session at Suzuka's Japanese Grand Prix. Russell pipped Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli by a tiny margin. Lando Norris had a slower start to practice, having a rake fitted to his car to conduct aerodynamic testing.

Mario Andretti says he has 'tremendous respect' for Colton Herta. Herta has stepped away from the IndyCar Series to pursue his F1 dream. The American currently serves as the test driver for the Cadillac F1 team.

McLaren team chief Andrea Stella says the team are making progress. Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris qualified in third and fifth respectively. Stella says he would be "surprised" if McLaren could challenge Ferrari for a podium finish.

Ferrari has been the closest challenger to the factory Mercedes outfit in the 2026 season, sitting second in the championship and 31 points behind the dominant Silver Arrows. McLaren is third on only 18 points with three DNS’ across Melbourne and Shanghai with various mechanical issues hitting.

Kimi Antonelli secured pole position for the Japanese Grand Prix on Saturday. Team-mate George Russell will join him on the front row with a P2 start. Sky Sports F1 analyst Karun Chandhok says Antonelli has had the "upper hand" in practice.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc fumed over team radio after qualifying. The Monegasque driver qualified fourth for the Japanese Grand Prix. The FIA made a tweak to the qualifying rules for Japan, altering the maximum permitted energy recharge from nine megajoules to eight.

Max Verstappen was 10th fastest in qualifying for the Japanese Grand Prix. The Red Bull driver was outqualified by team-mate Isack Hadjar in Q2. The Dutchman will start tomorrow's race from 11th on the grid.

Kimi Antonelli will start on pole for the 2026 Formula 1 Japanese Grand Prix. The Italian will be joined on the front row by Red Bull's Max Verstappen. Alexander Albon and Carlos Sainz were knocked out in the first session.

Kimi Antonelli secures his second career pole position at the Japanese Grand Prix. The Ferrari driver beat Mercedes team-mate George Russell by three tenths. Red Bull's Max Verstappen was eliminated in Q2, with Arvid Lindblad 10th.

Scott Speed made his Formula 1 debut in 2006 with Toro Rosso. The American's F1 career only lasted 1.5 years with 28 total starts. Looking back, he admitted that there were plenty of things he would have changed if he could do it all over again.

Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad qualifies 10th for Japanese Grand Prix. Briton knocked out four-time champion Max Verstappen in Q3. F1 release onboard footage of Lindblad touching his car to the halo.

Norris will start Sunday’s race in fifth having qualified six tenths off polesitter Kimi Antonelli, who was around four tenths ahead of third-placed Piastri. McLaren was forced into replacing his electric motor causing Norris to only appear halfway through the one-hour session.

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has warned that George Russell will face similar issues during the Japanese Grand Prix to those he battled against in qualifying. Wolff confirmed after qualifying that changes had been made to Russell's car ahead of today's session at the Suzuka circuit.

Max Verstappen is openly reconsidering his future in Formula 1. The Red Bull driver was eliminated in Q2 at the Japanese Grand Prix. Verstappen has expressed unabashed aversion towards F1's new regulations. The 28-year-old has raced GT3 machinery in the Nurburgring Langstrecken-Serie.

Lewis Hamilton surprised fans at a Yokohama car meet in a Ferrari F40. The seven-time champion pulled up beside a Subaru Impreza and a Honda NSX. Hamilton also used his time ahead of the Japanese Grand Prix to take a samurai lesson with the artist who choreographed the Kill Bill fighting scenes.

Cadillac beat Aston Martin to 19th and 20th on the grid of the Japanese Grand Prix. Sergio Perez was the faster Cadillac driver on Saturday, with a 1m32.206s. Valtteri Bottas was 0.124s slower than his team-mate after pushing perhaps a bit too hard.

The 2026 power unit compromises which have yielded some action-packed racing so far have also destroyed the essence of qualifying. F1 has a couple of weeks to figure itself out before May's Miami Grand Prix amid talks between the FIA, F1 and the teams. The more drivers use the throttle, the more they are effectively punished by losing time on the straights.

Lando Norris was frustrated by the yo-yo effect of the power unit. Max Verstappen says the Suzuka layout made it difficult to time an overtake. The Red Bull driver believes the racing inside the car is not as authentic as it should be.

The safety implications of Formula 1's new technical regulations have rocketed to the top of the agenda after Oliver Bearman's massive accident in the Japanese Grand Prix. The Haas driver had been a second behind Franco Colapinto when the gap narrowed suddenly and unexpectedly because of a huge difference in electrical boost as they approached the Spoon corner.

The truck was on its way from Italy to Poland when it was stolen. KitKat has been a partner of Formula 1 since the start of the 2025 season. The company added that "the vehicle and its contents remain unaccounted for" An investigation is ongoing with local authorities.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri finished second in the 2026 Japanese Grand Prix. But who do you think was the best driver in the season opener? Vote in our poll below to find out who you think should be Driver of the Day.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen frustrated with Formula 1's current regulations. The Dutchman was unable to pass Alpine's Pierre Gasly on Suzuka's start-finish straight. The 2026 regulations introduced a near 50:50 split between internal combustion engine and electrical power.

Kimi Antonelli has taken a nine-point lead in the Formula 1 championship. Kimi Antonelli won from pole at the Chinese and Japanese grands prix. George Russell finished fourth at the Japanese Grand Prix. The Briton is not concerned by Antonelli taking the championship lead.

Kimi Antonelli wins Japanese Grand Prix after safety car intervention. Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc finish second and third respectively. Max Verstappen finishes seventh for Red Bull. Lance Stroll retires due to suspected water pressure.

Mercedes' George Russell added a sticker to his helmet for the Japanese Grand Prix. The sticker featured a holographic-style illustration of Russell alongside his self-proclaimed number one Japanese fan doing the now-famous T pose. The sticker follows in the footsteps of Williams driver Carlos Sainz, who kept a sticker from a fan on his helmet from the 2025 Azerbaijan Grand Prix until the end of the season.

Isack Hadjar finished 12th at the Japanese Grand Prix. The Red Bull driver lost three places in the first two laps of the race. The Frenchman said his car was 'undriveable' and 'dangerous' The Frenchman has scored just four points over the first three rounds of the season.

Kimi Antonelli claims his second consecutive pole in Suzuka. Oscar Piastri finishes second for McLaren. Lewis Hamilton leads the drivers' championship. Red Bull is now a midfield team in F1, according to Oleg Karpov.

Haas driver Ollie Bearman crashed out of the Japanese Grand Prix. The Briton crashed into the barriers at Spoon Curve on Lap 22. Bearman was seen limping away from the wreck and heading to the medical centre. Haas has confirmed that the driver didn't sustain a fracture after x-rays.

Kimi Antonelli is the youngest driver in history to lead the world championship. The Italian will carry a nine-point lead into the month of April. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton are third and fourth. Mercedes further extends its lead over Ferrari and McLaren in the constructors' championship.

Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli won the 2026 Japanese Grand Prix on Sunday. The 19-year-old has now won two races in a row for the German team. Team principal Toto Wolff was asked if he was a 'genius' by Natalie Pinkham.

Franco Colapinto says closing speeds in Formula 1 in 2026 can become ‘really dangerous’ after Oliver Bearman’s 50G crash at the Japanese Grand Prix. The Haas driver was approximately one second behind Colapinto through Suzuka’s sector two, before suddenly closing at Spoon.
